region.text: the Aleppo region, where the Mitanni army engaged the Egyptians

ledger.note: 1445: Mitanni meets Thutmose III at Aleppo. 'By Thutmose's 35th year, the king of Mitanni had raised a large army and engaged the Egyptians around Aleppo' (Thutmose III page, reopened 2026-10-19). The page gives regnal years only; year 35 = 1445 as new-kingdom-of-egypt /ledger/7 computes it, which this event mirrors (reviewer thin item).

1438 (bridged): the fighting over the Aleppo region ends with Thutmose III's last Syrian campaign. The Thutmose III page says only that 'Sometime before Thutmose's 42nd year, Mitanni apparently began spreading revolt among all the major cities in Syria' and gives no peace; the year mirrors new-kingdom-of-egypt /ledger/8.

ledger.note: c. 1350 BC: Ashur-uballit I annexes Mitanni territory. The page dates him '(1365–1330 BC)' and has him annex it 'in the middle of the 14th century BC'; it names no cities, so the region is the part of the 1400 shape that neither the 1300 rump nor the Hittite share holds.

region.text: Aleppo, Mukiš and Mitanni's lands west of the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1345 BC: Suppiluliuma I's war. 'The Hittite-Syrian war is dated to 1345 BC'; 'the western portions of its territory came under direct control of the Hittites'; Washukanni was sacked in the war. The Suppiluliuma page lists Aleppo, Mukiš and Isuwa among the One-Year War's conquests without a year.

c. 1330 BC: Mitanni becomes the rump state of Hanigalbat. 'The middle part continued on as the rump state of Hanigalbat'; Shattiwaza, installed by a Hittite army 'in the late 14th century BC' and reigning 'c. 1330–1305 BC', ruled it as a Hittite dependent. The year is the reign's start, bridged; the page does not date the name.

c. 1330: Shattiwaza rules Mitanni as a Hittite vassal. A Hittite army 'installed Shattiwaza, the son of Tushratta, as their vassal king of Mitanni' 'in the late 14th century BC' and he 'reigned c. 1330–1305 BC' (Mitanni page, reopened 2026-10-19). Mitanni is the vassal and the Hittites the suzerain; this mirrors hittites /ledger/8 (reviewer fix).
1327 BC: Carchemish falls. 'Carchemish too was taken after a siege'; the page dates it 'in 1327 BC'. The Suppiluliuma page has him install his son Piyaššili as vassal king.

c. 1305 (bridged): the Hittite suzerainty over the rump ends with Shattiwaza's reign. The page ends his reign c. 1305 and has Adad-nirari I capture Shattuara (reign 'c. 1305–1285 BC'), with no year for the change of suzerain; mirrors hittites /ledger/10. Between this year and the Assyrian vassalage at -1300 the rump has no suzerain on the map.

'Adad-nirari claims to have captured King Shattuara and brought him to Ashur, where he took an oath as a vassal'; 'he was allowed to return to Mitanni, where he paid Adad-nirari regular tribute' (Mitanni page, reopened 2026-10-19). The page gives Shattuara 'c. 1305–1285 BC' and Adad-nirari I 'c. 1307–1275 BC' but no year for the oath; -1300 lies inside that window and matches Cliopatria's shape step and assyria /ledger/15. Mitanni is the vassal and Assyria the suzerain; the vassal runs to the annexation of -1250.

region.text: Washukanni (Tell Fekheriye) and the Khabur headwaters; Kahat (Tell Barri) lies east of the shape and is not cut

ledger.note: c. 1300 (bridged): the Assyrians take Washukanni with the Khabur cities. 'Wasashatta ... attempted to rebel' and the Assyrians 'took Washukanni, Amasakku, Kahat, Shuru, Nabula, Hurra and Shuduhu as well' (Mitanni page). The page puts this in Wasashatta's reign ('c. 1285-1265 BC') and Adad-nirari I's (to 1275), i.e. 1285-1275, not 1300; -1300 is used to match assyria /ledger/15 ('several cities alongside the Khabur river', Cliopatria's step). Only Washukanni (Tell Fekheriye) is cut out: the gazetteer puts Kahat (Tell Barri, 36.739 N 41.127 E on the Tell Barri page) and 81 of the 83 cells of Hasaka governorate east of Cliopatria's 1300 rump (its edge is 40.35 E), inside the 'eastern lands' already lost at -1350, so a Kahat circle would move no cell of this state. The seat leaves the state with Washukanni.

wars.name: Egyptian campaigns against Mitanni (Thutmose III)
wars.outcome: The Egyptian army crossed the Euphrates at Carchemish; no land changed hands and Mitanni later made peace with Egypt under Thutmose IV and Amenhotep III.
wars.note: The page gives Thutmose III's 33rd year, not a BC year; 1447 is computed from his reign 1479–1425. The ledger now carries the Egyptian dossier's contest over the Aleppo region (-1445..-1438, Thutmose III page, year 35).

wars.name: Mitanni's sack of Assur
wars.outcome: Shaushtatar 'sacked the Assyrian capital of Assur'; no territorial change is recorded.
wars.note: The page dates it only 'some time in the 15th century during the reign of Nur-ili'; the Hittite summary gives c. 1450. No lasting territorial change is drawn.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: one row, -1500..-1241, 3 shapes. The infobox gives Established c. 1600 BC (new keyframe -1600, Khabur headwaters only, the page gives no early extent) and disestablished c. 1260, the text puts the last rebellion c. 1250; the dossier ends in -1250 (Cliopatria -1241; the Assyrian dossier has the final annexation at -1244). TIMING: Cliopatria cuts the kingdom from 181,339 to 48,683 km2 only at -1300; the pages date the Assyrian cut to the middle of the 14th century and the Hittite cuts to 1345 and 1327, so three new keyframes (-1350, -1345, -1327) and four losses carry it. The eastern and western shares are set differences of Cliopatria's own shapes, not page boundaries. ASSYRIAN DOSSIER DATES: it has Ashur-uballit I's conquest c. 1363, the Khabur cities at -1300 (Adad-nirari I, Cliopatria's step) and the last annexation at -1244; this dossier uses the Mitanni page's 'middle of the 14th century' (-1350), Washukanni at -1300 as a bridged loss that matches the Assyrian dossier's step (the page puts the capture in Wasashatta's reign, c. 1285-1265, under Adad-nirari I to 1275) and -1250 for the last. AREA: no infobox area. PAGE BUDGET: two pages (Mitanni, Suppiluliuma I); the Hittite dossier cites the Mitanni page too. NOT DRAWN: the Egyptian crossing of the Euphrates (Thutmose III, 33rd year) as a contest, because the page gives no Mitanni-held ground and the Egyptian dossier already records 1445–1438; Kizzuwatna's allegiance to Mitanni; Assyria as a Mitanni vassal c. 1430-1363 (me-02 asks for it; the Shaushtatar page says Mitanni made Assur a vassal but gives no year, and a vassal_start with counterpart assyria in this ledger would read as Mitanni being the vassal, as at -1300). COUNTERPARTS WANTED: kizzuwatna, syrian-city-states, nuzi/arrapha (Hurrian vassal states east of the Tigris), isuwa. The infobox lists 'Hittite Empire; Yamhad' as predecessors, which does not match the dates (the Hittites sacked Aleppo in the 16th century); no predecessor is claimed here. FIX PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer verdict fail): added the Hittite vassalage -1330..-1305 (mirror of hittites /ledger/8, /10), the Assyrian vassalage -1300..-1250, the -1300 loss of Washukanni to assyria (Kahat, whose coordinates the Tell Barri page gives, lies east of Cliopatria's 1300 rump, so no Kahat circle is cut), the Egyptian contest -1445..-1438 (Thutmose III page, mirror of new-kingdom-of-egypt /ledger/7-8), the -1300 keyframe now adjust, the Washukanni capital ending -1301. Direction of the vassal events: Mitanni is the vassal, the counterpart the suzerain, as the reviewer asks. NOT CHANGED: the final annexation stays at -1250 (Shattuara II's rebellion 'around 1250 BC'; assyria /ledger/16 has -1244, to be moved to -1250 by me-02); the -1500 gain from assyria (Shaushtatar page: no year for the sack of Assur; c. 1450 is the author's war date) and the Hanigalbat rename -1330 (Hanigalbat page: no start date). DISAGREEMENT: the page dates the capture of the Khabur cities to 1285-1275, not -1300; kept at -1300 so that the two ledgers agree, and if both are moved they should move together. Pages opened in the fix pass: Mitanni, Tell Barri, Hanigalbat, Shaushtatar, Thutmose III (four over the 1-2 page budget, for the reviewer's thin items and the Kahat coordinates). CELL CHECK (gazetteer, fix pass): Cliopatria's 1300 rump spans 37.3-40.35 E; the Hasaka governorate that assyria /ledger/15 gains at -1300 has 83 cells, of which only 1 is in the rump and 81 are in this dossier's -1350 loss to assyria. So the Khabur cities are lost here 50 years before the page's capture (Wasashatta) and assyria's -1300 gain overlaps this -1350 loss; me-02 and the orchestrator should decide whether to move the Hasaka cells from -1350 to -1300 in both ledgers (page: 'The kingdom had by now been reduced to the Khabur Valley', which the Cliopatria rump does not match).
